English: Timber Slipway
A basic wooden ramp for launching and hauling smaller boats, constructed by the faithful to aid in river or coastal activity and modest pilgrim traffic.
Boat Landing
A makeshift dock and gathering area, where pilgrims and clergy can disembark safely. Simple, but brings the faithful closer to the water and each other.
Wooden Dock
A sturdier wooden dock for modest vessels, supporting pilgrim arrivals, temple processions, and small-scale naval activities under the temples auspices.
Covered Boathouse
A fortified, roofed boathouse for protecting sacred vessels and housing clergy engaged in seaborne ministry, with space for workshops and religious gatherings.
Stone Wharf
A professionally built stone wharf, allowing for the berthing of larger ships and greater volumes of religious travelers, trade, and temple influence.
Shipbuilders Shed
A dedicated workshop for repairing and crafting ships, employing skilled craftsmen in service of the faith. Improves naval readiness and religious maritime influence.
Reinforced Shipyard
A heavily fortified shipyard with stone walls, workshops, and barracks for religious guards. Ensures the protection of temple ships and asserts ecclesiastical authority over the port.
Dry Dock
A permanent dry dock, enabling the construction and maintenance of large vessels dedicated to the faith. Attracts skilled labor and increases regional prosperity and security.
Expanded Dockyards
A vast expansion of the shipyard, with multiple docks, warehouses, and housing for pilgrims, clergy, and craftsmen. A regional center of religious, economic, and naval power.
Grand Shipyard Complex
A sprawling, monumental shipyard complex, the pride of the religious community. Capable of supporting pilgrim fleets, crusading flotillas, and international religious trade.
